meta.title: Four Steps to Melon with Cream

paragraphs: On Monday, April fifth, the cooking course started at nine o'clock. Chef Lucy waited in the community center kitchen next to the library. Lily, Mia, and May wore white aprons and stood at a long steel table. On the table were the ingredients: a melon, a bowl of coconut cream, and a bowl of sugar. "Today we make melon with cream in four steps," said Chef Lucy. "This recipe is easy, and the dish is tasty." "Wash your hands first," she said. "Does everyone know how to use a knife?" The girls washed their hands at the sink.

A board on the wall showed four numbered drawings. Chef Lucy read the instructions slowly. "First, cut the melon in half and scoop out the seeds." "Next, cut the melon into small pieces." "Then mix one cup of cream with two spoons of sugar." "After that, pour the cream on the melon, and set the bowl in the fridge." "Serve it cold after twenty minutes." "What does 'scoop' mean?" asked May. Lily looked at the spoon in her hand. "I think that it means to take out with a spoon," she said. "Yes," said Chef Lucy. "The seeds are scooped out with a spoon." The girls followed the steps one by one. Mia cut a thin slice of melon and tasted it. "It is tasty already," she said.

In the evening, Leo asked Lily to send the recipe to his pen pal Ravi. Lily sat at her laptop and wrote an email. Next to the laptop lay her notebook with a drawing of a melon. "Dear Ravi, here are the four steps from Chef Lucy." "First, cut the melon in half and scoop out the seeds." "Next, cut it into small pieces." "Then mix one cup of cream with two spoons of sugar." "After that, pour the cream on the melon, and set the bowl in the fridge." "Serve it cold after twenty minutes." "Best wishes, Lily." Ravi answered in a few minutes. "Dear Lily, thank you!" "I will cook it on Saturday." "Best wishes, Ravi."

Then Ravi wrote again with a question. "Dear Lily, what does 'set' mean in the last step?" "Do I put the bowl on top of the fridge?" Lily laughed and wrote an answer. "Dear Ravi, 'set' means 'put' here." "Put the bowl inside the fridge, not on top." "Best wishes, Lily."
Lily closed the laptop and looked at her drawing. "On Wednesday, Chef Lucy will teach a new dish," she said. "I hope that it is as easy as melon," she added.
